rationale: C07 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Beyond the standard emergency-board structure shared by many candidates, it concerns an airline dispute involving the same union and uses the directly adaptable formulation “Flight Engineers' International Association, UAL Chapter,” which the child converts to “Flight Engineers' International Association, EAL Chapter.” It also follows the same sequence of predicates, thirty-day reporting requirement, and section 10 status-quo provision. C10 is strong because it concerns airlines including Eastern Airlines and closely matches the operative structure, while C22 is a recent, same-administration example with nearly identical phrasing and capitalization, but neither has C07's distinctive union-and-chapter correspondence.

shared_material.parent_excerpt: United Air Lines, Inc. ... employees represented by the Flight Engineers' International Association, UAL Chapter
shared_material.explanation: The same airline-specific union description and carrier-initial chapter designation are adapted to a different airline.
